Homonyms can be defined as two or more words that share the same spelling, or the same pronunciation, or both, but have different meanings. It is an umbrella term that includes other types of words like homophones and heteronyms.
Homophones are two or more words that share the same pronunciation but have different meanings and spellings. They may or may not be spelled the same way.
Heteronyms are homonyms that share the same spelling but have different pronunciations.

images.text:
Giving Effective Feedback
  • Address the behavior, not the person. Open by stating the behavior in question, then describing how you feel about it, and end by stating what you want. This model enables you to focus on behaviors rather than on your assumptions. Example: “I haven't seen you at our board meetings lately. I'm worried that you are missing important information. Can we meet soon to discuss it?” rather than “You obviously don't think our board meetings are important!”

• Balance the content. Use the “sandwich approach”. Begin by providing comments on specific strengths, to give reinforcement and identify things the recipient should be doing. Then identify specific areas for improvement and ways to make changes. Conclude with a positive comment. Example: “Your speech was great. You made good eye contact and were well prepared. You were a little hard to hear at the back of the room, but with some practice you can overcome this. Keep up the good work!” Instead of: “You didn't speak loudly enough, but otherwise the speech went well.”

• Be specific. Avoid general comments that may be of limited use to the receiver. Try to include examples to illustrate your statements. Remember, too, that offering alternatives rather than just giving advice allows the receiver to decide what to do with your feedback.
  • Be realistic. Feedback should focus on what can be changed. It is frustrating for recipients to get comments on things over which they have no control.
